reviews.text: At least a proper turn based game! I've been waiting for such a game for years. Both Darkest Dungeon and Iratus were a bit off for me. First too randomy, second a bit too stuffed and easy. A very nice combination of character skills and equipment. It is hard enough and has a proper challenge on hardcore difficulty. Liked the art-style and animation, for an indie game without a publisher feels good. Especially nice touch with the lively backgrounds at the first boss. Wonder why more developers don't do that in their games. Music and sounds too, they hit the mark for me. It does take a bit of reading skills and understanding the combat mechanics. Also characters need a few levels to open up. There are many ways to compose your squad combining character abilities with each other, the combo mechanic is awesome once you learn to use it properly. There is a lot of depth in the game. I'd say a very good potential. And a solid EA start! Didn't like all the texts popping up in the combat, but found you can turn all floating texts off in the setting menu. Didn't play much yet (1.5 hours), but so far it is wonderful. Checks all the boxes. No bugs or crashes so far. My rig is an older one still runs perfectly with maxed out rendering and stuff. Definitely a must play for any and all turn based lovers out there.

Played it for an hour so far, very addicting game. Wanted to eat, had to settle with dead bugs. Wanted to relieve myself, had to do a cartman. I do not understand how or why but ,y wife from the command center sends me out on missions, just like in real life, feels right at home. And the dude with the cigar is just like my father, never a kind word, just do that do this. Only the bugs understand me, the warm embrace of the big tanky ones feels like my pals from the dungeon. And the master at the hangar shouts just like the dungeon master. + Feels like home. + My wifu in the com center orders me around like irl. + Hardcore warms my sacred ring like the boys in my dungeon. + Bugs swarm as when i enter my room. The character progression does not let me leave the game. Nice synergies and skill trees. Battles are quite fun, especially when you level up your squad a bit. Looking forward to see how it plays further. Want to see upgraded classes. Want to see new locations. Looking for new enemies. - Can't undress my wifu. - Can't punch my dad, i mean the military guy. - Social rating... I heard it somewhere before. Doesn't look like a bright future tbh. - They promise only around 30+ hours gameplay for the EA start. Overall it is worth 300 bucks in my opinion. So I give it nine dungeon master out of 10 dungeons.

这是一款回合制RPG游戏。 游戏的画面就场景看着还行，立绘有简单Live2D，但是角色建模就和纸片一样，虽然说暗黑地牢也是角色有点纸片，但是美术很好的弥补了这个问题，但是本作的纸片看着就像是粗糙的手游素材，总体来说较为简陋。 背景就是飞船在一个未知星球坠毁，然后虫子攻破了飞船，主角在冷冻仓被唤醒之后就开始战斗，按照舰长要求完成任务，最好拯救飞船上的所有人。 玩法上战斗部分类似暗黑地牢，玩家在地图上走（分支路线少），然后遇敌就会进入回合制战斗，根据先攻值来决定先后顺序。 流程是关卡制的，每一次都会遇敌四五次，然后打一个boss就算结束了。 养成部分角色可以升级，有多种装备，转职的分支多，还多种天赋树。 通过消耗资源解锁飞船的设施，回复角色疲劳值，从冷冻仓唤醒新的高等级角色，购买并装备新的武器，护甲和道具。 战斗还是有点难的，就算选最简单的难度，一次战斗也要打上近10分钟，打赢之后经验还不能当场结算，需要通关之后才会结算并升级。 我觉得比较蠢的一点就是动态等级的设置，我略施小计，直接拉出了高等级角色，然后准备带着几个低价角色准备去刷下级，结果1个12级带着3个1级的，遇到的敌人直接都是7级的，直接把我低级角色都杀了，我当时人都麻了，估计是制作组为了保证游戏难度才这么干的，但是这样弄感觉一点意思都没有了。 有中文，但是全是机翻，什么boss翻译成老板，技能名字出现“应该翻译为迅捷攻击”，舰长一会管主角叫孩子，一会叫儿子，我都不知道用的到底是什么牌子的翻译--GPT真的没有这么蠢的，试试看好吗？ 总结 从冷冻仓唤醒新角色那部分搞得和手游抽卡似的，所以真的不是什么手游素材再利用吗？ 总之玩起来就感觉麻烦的不得了，建议就是骨折之后当成喜加一购买。 [quote]游玩百态，将游玩心得用汉语化作玩家的指明灯 [url=https://store.steampowered.com/curator/35402408/]点击这里关注汉化语录~[/url] 如果喜欢这个评测，请点个赞让更多人看见[/quote]

Lovely game if a bit rough around the edges. I would describe the game as Darkest Dungeon meets Starship Troopers. I especially like the combat system. It appears simple at first but quickly ramps up in complexity with interesting combat mehcanics that encourage a lot of interactions between characters builds or enemy types. Also devs seem eager to work on the game, and have already implemented some fixes and qol improvements with quite a bunch more to come. I say you should wait for an update or two first but definitely recommend the game overall.

[h1]星际巡航队[/h1] 这是一款横版异星探索题材的回合制战斗冒险游戏。我们将从众多角色中组建最多为4人的小队征战各种探索任务。每个角色都有着自己独特的职业、技能和可以穿戴的装备。流程上是关卡制，玩家控制的小队在一路前行会遇敌触发战斗。战斗机制本质上比较简单，就是异常状态实在是有些眼花缭乱，加上汉化的质量堪忧，导致有一定的理解门槛。不过回合制战斗本身的乐趣还是不错的，虽然比较墨迹，但对策略搭配和出招时机却有一定的要求。 [h1]游戏体验[/h1] 游戏的画面是美式的异星球机械风，虽然不能说十分精细，但是观感上倒还是挺炫酷的。横版的滚轴画面中也有多图层的设计，你时常能在战斗中看到同轴画面位置还有很多的第三方人物甚至是事件。虽然你无法与之产生互动，但是对于沉浸感的提升是有的。 战斗方面随着移动而强制遇敌，因此也没有载入或者是画面切换界面。可以最多上阵四人，拖拽头像可变更队列位置，每个角色有着最多6个技能。类型上涉及AOE、单体以及一些判定距离的技能。伤害数值平平无奇，主打的是眼花缭乱的BUFF。敌人身上挂个四五个DEBUFF是常有的事情，这也使得游戏的节奏比较慢。 除了常规属性外，角色有着一个先攻值，行动后可以进行累计。数值到150的时候可以进行双重攻击，往往可以扭转战局，不过可笑的是机翻成了“双重转身”。 [h1]总结[/h1] 还算不错的横版卷轴回合制游戏。但是目前的各种翻译问题还是非常严重，建议正式版发布前润色下。 [quote]欢迎关注我们的鉴赏家:[url=https://store.steampowered.com/curator/35402982/]走心评测[/url] ←遵从内心，写出真实感受 欢迎加入我们Steam组:[url=https://steamcommunity.com/groups/ZXPC]走心评测[/url]←点击加入，一起探索游戏的乐趣 喜欢这篇评论，也麻烦点个赞，让更多人能够看到！[/quote]

[h1]科幻风的《暗黑地牢》！就问你爱不爱！[/h1] 《Tenebris: Terra Incognita》是由Phantasmica Studios自研自发的一款横版科幻小队回合制战斗冒险游戏。游戏里主角所在的飞船遭受外星生物袭击紧急迫降在不知名星球，船长将身为战士的主角从休眠中唤醒，并让他组建队队伍护卫飞船，顺便探索异形，我们的冒险就从这时开始！ 游戏的画面有点美式科幻风，各种角色、装备、场景、乃至UI都有着相当不错的科技感，不过角色立绘虽然有那么一点立体感，却有那么一点AI绘制的感觉，不过这并不影响我们的良好的游戏体验就是了！ 游戏的游玩机制有点《暗黑地牢》的感觉，同样是组建四个不同职业的角色队伍进行横版冒险，不同的是我们需要在战斗中搜索敌人尸体或路边的尸体、闪光物来获取各种“生物材料”，这算是游戏的主要货币的一种，可以在战后飞船上让经常出击的队员在医疗站和冷冻中心使用获得休整恢复疲劳值等。 游戏里各角色都有着自己的职业、技能、天赋树和属于各职业的装备，战斗和探索最大的乐趣就是刷到各种不同等级等阶的装备，这种刷刷刷的感觉并不比专门的刷宝游戏来的差。游戏的战斗主要以回合制进行，相对比较简单，就是双方轮流出手，我方作为高科技装备加身的战士有着护盾不稀奇，稀奇的是虫族敌人竟然也有护盾，外星生物果然恐怖如斯！不过需要注意的是各种各样让人眼花缭乱的状态BUFF和DEBUFF，一堆挂身上的时候分分钟下回合动一下就挂了，虽说可以在胜利后救治倒下的队员，但那可都是需要花费资源的，因此认真计算这些状态会带来的后果相当重要！这也让本来节奏就不快的战斗变得更为拖拽，是好是坏只能看玩家时候有很好的策略心情了！ 整体来说，《Tenebris: Terra Incognita》算是一款相当不错的回合制角色探险游戏，用科幻战斗的角度来体验不一样的《暗黑地牢》，优秀的机制也值得玩家探索，就是这翻译嘛！机翻太严重了，建议制作组在这方面稍微增加点心思？！~ [quote]关注[url=https://store.steampowered.com/curator/36224058/]老实人鉴赏家 [/url] [url=https://steamcommunity.com/groups/laoshirenLSR]老实人评测[/url]：独立游戏爱好者聚集地，黄油绅士交流中心。 不错过游戏的亮点，不放过游戏的槽点，带给玩家最直观的测评感受。[/quote]

怎么说呢？先说说缺点，这游戏目前由于是抢先体验阶段肯定会有点不完善，BUG我也遇到了几个，关于中文机翻问题也严重，我调整了一下中英文发现有些技能描述和效果都翻译错了。 但是整个游戏底子还是很不错的，制作组态度很不错，也非常认真的对待社区里的反馈，回合间卡死的BUG在反馈后也很快修复了。在我反馈之后甚至也会认真用中文回复我的关于BUG和翻译错误的反馈，制作组回复了我关于翻译错误这一点：因为是非常小且独立的制作组，没钱还是兼职做游戏，所以说暂且只能使用机翻翻译其他语言，在后面更新中会请专业的翻译公司翻译其他语言。其他恶性的影响游戏进行的BUG修复的也很快。 接下来说说游戏本身，这个游戏是一个类暗黑地牢的回合制战术游戏，每个角色的可以按照配装和技能搭配出不同的定位配合其他角色打出各种各样的套路（我自己就配出来一个一个暴击可以打出178伤害的逆天毒奶），小队装备和技能成型之后就是一爽游，只要不浪就是嘎嘎乱杀，我稍微浅玩了35个小时，打到了现在版本的最终点。然后发了这个评测，打算等后面的更新。毕竟还是早期体验游戏要有耐心。 看路线图可以看出来后面更新要很慢，但是制作组态度决定了一切，完整游戏一定是一个好游戏，好游戏是需要时间去做的，你如果愿意支持制作组，可以现在就入手支持一下制作组，也可以选择观望一下。看看这个游戏的未来会走向何方。

This is a great game. The best way to describe it is "Sci-fi Darkest Dungeon." Major inspirations seem to be Space Marines along with Starship Troopers and/or Aliens. Indie games like this can sometimes feel disjointed when it comes to the overall vibe and tone. Happy to say that that is not the case with Tenebris: everything from the artwork and sound design to the gameplay loop create a really unified feel that makes it satisfying. This is definitely a "one more run" game where the next thing you know it's 2am. I really love the artwork in Tenebris--specifically the character and enemy artwork. You can tell right away from the design of each bug what it's going to do. Huge pincers? It's gonna stab you with them. Big bloated sac on its abdomen? Yeah, that thing is spray acid goo at you. The bugs are terrifying in the best way--so you won't have a problem mowing down rows and rows of them (my personal favorite is cleansing them with fire). The five base classes are unique but also cover a bit of similar ground so its easy to make a party of four that covers all the bases. I especially like the advanced classes as they each feel distinct and also build on the qualities that made the base classes work. Visually they look great and the artwork again does a good job of telling you what each character does. The level design really worked for me. While its a simple 2-D scroll like in Darkest Dungeon, you have to keep an eye out for collectibles, chest etc. The devs did a great job making the most of the environment despite how limited it might seem. From eerie mountains in the background, to weird alien particles floating through the air, to foreground stalagmites in the claustrophobic cave levels, every part of the level design comes together to make memorable locales. I have a few gripes with the gameplay. The base upgrades feel very hit or miss--some are must pick ASAP and others seem like a big investment for minimal gain. I encourage the devs to think about ways to make each upgrade feel impactful, rather than a bunch of +10% benefits here and there. Two other small issues are not enough space on the hotbar for abilities and way too many equipment drops that don't do anything. I am happy to see that these are both being addressed in the 1.0 release, so these are only temporary gripes. The early access feels like a mostly complete game, and I would recommend it in its current state any day of the week. The fact that there will be a full release with more advanced classes, biomes etc, down the road is a huge bonus.

So if you stick with one squad on higher difficulties the game is fine. The problem is that, ostensibly, you will need more than one squad at some point as there is a fatigue rating which means that you will have to take them out of rotation whilst they recuperate. The fact we have more than a minimum squad also suggests they are expendable. I like impactful failures resulting in catastrophic conditions like death but only providing they are earned due my own lack of forethought, attention to detail, mistakes, or ignorance and not a result of RNG, scripted narrative, or conditions beyond my control. It is also nice when there is the ability to recover, regardless of difficulty, from such outcomes. XCOM, as an example, was excellent in this regard even if it was prone to, shall we say, some intermittent and unlikely occurrences. If, however, you try to prepare for the anticipated need for future personnel by using your higher level squad for away missions while using the new recruits for the training missions you will either lose some in the process or you will have to save scum the levels to get them through it. Maintaining parity of your units isn't merely difficult, it seems to be discouragingly prohibitive. The instructor isn't a tank and has no way to control aggro, meaning your entire squad is vulnerable all the time. Not that it matters since he spends an inordinate amount of combat being stunned because he seems to have absolutely no resistance beyond dodge to being staggered. The enemies prioritize weak armor and low hit points, which is the very definition of low level recruits. Additionally, and I am not exaggerating, more than half of the encounters are ambushes as a result of using new recruits with low initiative. Enemies invariably stun the high level mentor unit depriving him of his first turn (and more depending upon what random recruits you get, what gear you have for them, and how long combat lasts) then proceed to concentrate on one recruit at a time and kill them. On two fights, out of maybe ten, I lost one recruit each before they got a turn. By lost I mean he was downed for the encounter, but you can only being a unit back from being downed once per mission on which there seems be a half dozen to somewhere south of ten encounters in all. So it looks like these missions were balanced with the assumption players would bring their best and most experienced units. I would happily do so, except away missions seem to give no discernable experience whatsoever. On my first run I tasked my level one units on three missions and they were still level one at the end of them, while my advanced units were graining a minimum of a level and sometimes more than two on active missions. I had five units at level five and three at level one. That is a huge gap. Hence why I began again with the idea of fielding my low level units only to find out that while you can eke through the first training mission you get absolutely wrecked right out of the gate on the second one. By wrecked, I mean all three (level 2) recruits were downed in the very first fight while the mentor's armor hadn't even been broken yet because he was ignored except for stun attacks. I didn't bother to finish the missions since I felt confident the moment any of the recruits died I would simply be entering a death spiral which would eventually see the whole team wiped. It was obvious enough at that point I didn't really need to see it play out. I want a challenge, but units dying before they get turns, or only after a single turn, is mostly just disappointing since no combat on higher difficulties is determined in a single round with fresh recruits although if you know you are doing and with a little luck you can end most of them in two. Maybe I am being impatient. Maybe after the training missions there are multiple options to choose from which allow for grinding assets/experience/whatever at a comfortable pace. Maybe thinking ahead and trying to approach things strategically is actually working against me. Don't know, but since there are no hard saves, I am not able to experiment and discover these things for myself without starting everything all over again on a fresh run. . .And you know what, at this point I have put in too much time to want to start over, but not nearly enough to fall in love with this title. Especially since, at this point, I haven't even come within line of sight of a plot to all this yet. Shelving it for now, will return to it in a year or so. These are good devs, I am sure they will sort it out, but for now it is just not for me.

The game has a lot of potential with a few major issues. One of them is tedium. Lots of side missions that reward too little for literally 20-30 minutes of your real-life time. A few hours into the game, and my inventory is flooded with the same tier of boring starter weapons/armor. Another issue is the lack of system descriptions. For instance, a gene stimulator buff you can unluck to give your soldiers 25% more XP; however, it only lasts a single mission while taking about 1/3 of your total resources to activate, per soldier. Nowhere does it list a duration. This applies to many things in the game, including typos in descriptions. If the devs clean up the descriptions and make quests a bit more rewarding, the game has a ton of potential and I'd recommend it.

(Offline Steam doesn't count game play time) [h2]Wait On The Version 1.0 Update[/h2] The game itself is really well done, until you realize there are a lot of glaring flaws in it's design. The forcing you to have multiple squads, one decked out, and one underleveled, having to switch them out sequentially, and forcing you into repeated runs of lower stages to gear them up but without a game play speed up toggle (coming in v1.0) it just bores you. You can save scum to revive your squad, which trust me, if you have chosen a higher difficulty you will want to do, for multiple reasons. You can save scum deaths, loot boxes at the start of a mission, run if you're about to die, among other things. It just feels like it's too slow, too safe and too unrewarding to play once you've reached the point where you can't progress anymore because it's early access. A shame. [h2]Conclusion[/h2] It's a perfectly fine game with good concepts, it just needs more updates and adjustments.
